competing_trace_defects.description: After selecting “Remove bookmark” for the visible Bulldog post at step 10, the trajectory treated that same still-rendered post as another remaining target at step 11; at step 12 it misread the menu label “Bookmark” and selected it, visibly changing the later menu state to “Remove bookmark.”

chains.rationale: At reuse step 13, the exposed claim that a final post still needed removal was explicitly followed by reopening that post’s menu, extending the redundant handling created by the prior menu misinterpretation. The resulting menu visibly said “Remove bookmark,” and step 14 selected that corrective option, interrupting and recovering from the mechanism. The post remains rendered in the Saved view afterward and no fresh menu or refreshed list verifies its bookmark state, so complete satisfaction of the predicate is not observably established.

summary: The reused false progress framing extended redundant processing of a previously handled #pets post, but the subsequent “Remove bookmark” action visibly corrected that mechanism. The final complete bookmark predicate is not directly verifiable from the static Saved view.
